description: The line plot, titled “BBQ,” illustrates the accuracy of four different methods—Squared exponential, Flash, ELU, and LLaMA-2-chat-7B—as a function of the number of demonstrations, ranging from 0 to 1500 on the x-axis. The x-axis, labeled “#Demonstrations,” is linearly scaled with major tick marks at intervals of 250. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” is also linearly scaled, ranging from 45 to 55, with major tick marks at intervals of 5. The “Squared exponential” method, represented by a dark blue line with circular markers and a solid line style, starts at approximately 53.5 accuracy at 0 demonstrations, rises to about 55.5 at 250 demonstrations, and then plateaus near 55.5 through 1500 demonstrations. The “Flash” method, shown as a medium blue line with circular markers and a solid line, begins near 49.5, dips slightly to ~49.0 at 250, then rises to ~50.5 at 500, and stabilizes near 50.5 through 1500. The “ELU” method, depicted as a light blue line with circular markers and a solid line, remains nearly flat across the entire range, hovering consistently around 47.5. The “LLaMA-2-chat-7B” method, shown as a lavender line with circular markers and a solid line, stays nearly constant near 46.5 from 0 to 1500 demonstrations. All lines are plotted with circular markers at each data point, and the legend is positioned in the upper right of the plot area.
